text: # Frontline Response to Network Outage Queries **Document ID:** TRN_002 **Category:** GENERAL — Cross-Category / General **Department:** Network **Customer Scope:** all **Last Updated:** 2026-07-30 **Version:** 1.0 **Source Authority:** Internal Knowledge Base --- ## Learning Objectives - Understand the customer scenario this module covers and why it matters. - Apply the correct process steps consistently and within SLA. - Recognise when to escalate rather than continue troubleshooting. ## Core Content # Frontline Response to Network Outage Queries **Document ID:** TRN_002 **Department:** Network **Category:** General (C01-C29) **Last Updated:** 2026-05-06 **Version:** 1.0 --- ## Learning Objectives Agents can check outage status tools, set correct customer expectations, and escalate P1 issues. ## Using the Outage Dashboard Agents must check the internal NOC dashboard (not just the customer-facing map, which may lag by up to 15 minutes) before confirming outage status to a customer. ## Setting Expectations Never commit to an exact restoration time unless it is published by NOC. Use ranges (e.g., 'within the next 4 hours') and offer SMS notification opt-in for restoration alerts. ## Escalation Trigger Any report suggesting >500 affected customers in one area that is not yet on the dashboard should be flagged to NOC immediately as a potential undetected outage. ## Key Definitions - **SLA** — the target time within which a request or issue should be resolved. - **Escalation** — handing a case to a specialist team when first-line steps do not resolve it. ## Worked Example During a routine interaction, the agent identifies this scenario, applies the
